title: Synthetic Division Calculator
description: Divide a polynomial by (x − c) with synthetic division: full tableau, bring-down / multiply / add steps, quotient and remainder.
howto: Type the dividend coefficients from highest degree to constant (e.g. 2 3 -4 1).
Type c — the value in the divisor (x − c).
Press Divide to see the tableau built step by step.
Read the quotient coefficients and the remainder from the bottom row.

faqs.a: A shortcut for dividing a polynomial by (x − c): bring down the leading coefficient, multiply by c, add to the next coefficient, repeat. The bottom row gives the quotient coefficients and the final remainder.
Write (x + 3) as (x − (−3)) and enter c = −3. The sign matters: always use the value subtracted from x.

faqs.q: What does the remainder tell me?
faqs.a: By the Remainder Theorem, the remainder equals P(c). If it is 0, then (x − c) is a factor of the polynomial.
